senses.gloss: m. (טלל, with format. ז or ס; cmp. אוּשְׁפֵּיז; v. טָלַל II, טְלַל I, II) a number of booths put up for a mercantile fair, or for popular entertainments; whence (cmp. חָנוּת) shops, bazaar (v. esp.
units: <cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 79">Gen. R. s. 79</cite>, quot. bel.).
<cite ref="Chullin 91b:5">Ḥull. 91ᵇ</cite> <he>א׳ של אמאוס</he> the fair of Emmaus. Pesik. Asser p. 98ᵇ.

<cite ref="Mishnah Arakhin 6:5">Arakh. VI, 5</cite> (<cite ref="Arakhin 24a:22">24ᵃ</cite>) <he>אם ממתינין אותה לאיטלס</he> if they delay the sale for the market day; a. fr.—Pl. <he>אַטְלֵסִין</he> &c.

Gen. R. s. 79 (ref. to ויחן ‘and he encamped’ = made a חנות Gen. XXXIII, 18) Jacob was the first מעמיד א׳ Ar. (ed. also הטלסין, v. הֶטְלֵיס) to put up stores and sell cheap; [Koh. R. to X, 8; Est. R. to I, 9, sing., some ed. אִיתְּלִיס, אַתְּלִיס (!)]. Cmp. עַטְלֵיז, אִסְטֵל [Tosef. Ḥull. I, 7 באטלס read באַטְלֵק by throwing; cmp.
